gateway_config_run:
# TASK-HANDLE gate: agentgateway in front of the practice task server, with
# PER-USER upstream identity. Ports are double-brace placeholders; the driver
# (integration/handle_gateway_gate.py) writes a port-substituted copy to a
# scratch dir and refuses to run with any placeholder left, or with a port
# outside its block. Everything is loopback-only: agentgateway binds all
# interfaces by default, so every listener is pinned to 127.0.0.1 and stats /
# readiness are off.
#   client --(user JWT)--> agentgateway 4601  (jwtAuth: local AS JWKS)
#   agentgateway --(the same validated user JWT, backendAuth.passthrough)-->
#     practice task server 4602/mcp
# The practice server identifies the caller by its Authorization header, so
# users A and B stay distinct at the upstream, which does the task owner check.
config:
  adminAddr: 127.0.0.1:4603
  statsAddr: "off"
  readinessAddr: "off"
gateways:
  handle:
    port: 4601
    bindAddress: 127.0.0.1
routes:
- name: handle-mcp
  gateways: handle
  policies:
    jwtAuth:
      mode: strict
      providers:
      - issuer: https://local-as.test
        audiences: [agentgateway-api]
        jwks:
          url: http://127.0.0.1:4600/jwks
  backends:
  - mcp:
      statefulMode: stateful
      targets:
      - name: tasks
        mcp:
          host: http://127.0.0.1:4602/mcp
        policies:
          backendAuth:
            passthrough: {}
upstream_auth: per-user passthrough: backendAuth.passthrough forwards the validated user JWT unchanged (a token-passthrough config)
